original_value: Mining human behaviors has always been an important subarea of Data Mining. While it provides empirical evidences to psychological/behavioral studies, it also builds the foundation of various big-data systems, which rely heavily on the prediction of human behaviors. In recent years, the ubiquitous spreading of mobile phones and the massive amount of spatio-temporal data collected from them make it possible to keep track of the daily commute behaviors of mobile subscribers and further conduct routine mining on them. In this article, we propose to model mobile subscribers’ daily commute behaviors by three levels: location trajectory, one-day pattern, and routine pattern. We develop the model Spatio-Temporal Routine Mining Model (STRMM) to characterize the generative process between these three levels. From daily trajectories, the STRMM model unsupervisedly extracts spatio-temporal routine patterns that contain two aspects of information: (1) How people’s typical commute patterns are. (2) How much their commute behaviors vary from day to day. Compared to traditional methods, STRMM takes into account the different degrees of behavioral uncertainty in different timespans of a day, yielding more realistic and intuitive results. To learn model parameters, we adopt Stochastic Expectation Maximization algorithm. Experiments are conducted on two real world datasets, and the empirical results show that the STRMM model can effectively discover hidden routine patterns of human commute behaviors and yields higher accuracy results in trajectory prediction task.

result.paraphrase: Mining human behavior has long been a key subfield of data mining. It not only offers empirical evidence for psychological and behavioral research, but also underpins many big-data systems that depend heavily on predicting human actions. In recent years, the widespread use of mobile phones and the large volumes of spatio-temporal data they generate have made it possible to monitor mobile subscribers’ daily commuting behavior and perform routine mining on it. This paper models mobile subscribers’ daily commute behavior at three levels: location trajectories, one-day patterns, and routine patterns. We propose the Spatio-Temporal Routine Mining Model (STRMM) to describe the generative relationship among these three levels. From daily trajectories, STRMM unsupervisedly extracts spatio-temporal routine patterns that capture two kinds of information: (1) what people’s typical commuting patterns are, and (2) how much their commute behavior varies from day to day. Compared with conventional methods, STRMM accounts for differing levels of behavioral uncertainty across different periods of the day, producing results that are more realistic and intuitive. Model parameters are learned using the Stochastic Expectation Maximization algorithm. Experiments on two real-world datasets show that STRMM can effectively uncover hidden routine patterns in human commuting behavior and achieves higher accuracy in trajectory prediction tasks.
